No propositions came through, so I can't pick among them. The strongest general objection I know is that the calculus needs pleasures and pains on one cardinal scale that can be compared across persons, and no such scale exists, so the "sum" of happiness is undefined. The team note's angle (whether pleasure and pain are unavoidable in every life) is weaker, because Bentham's claim is that they are the only motives and measures of value, and that is better attacked by examples like Nozick's experience machine than by asking whether they are universal.
